strengths: The WPDDFormer model consistently outperforms other state-of-the-art methods across multiple tasks on the JARVIS and Materials Project datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness.
The authors provide theoretical guarantees on the continuity and completeness of the WPDD-based graphs, ensuring robust performance under minor structural perturbations.
This work makes very significant novelty contributions in combining pairwise distance distribution with machine learning based crystal property prediction.
The quality of this work is evidenced by good theoretic analysis and strong experiment results.
The writing of this work is overall good and clear.
The idea of efficiently integrating pairwise distance distribution into transformer model proposed by this work is insightful and enlightning for researchers in borad AI for science community.
The proposed crystal representation demonstrates continuity under small distortions and perturbations, which can be advantageous for robustness.
The proposed (W/U)PDDs incorporate atomic information into PDD and address its high computational cost.
The paper is overall well-written with nice flow, clarity, and illustrations.
weaknesses: An ablation study on the effect of varying the radius on WPDDFormer’s performance and efficiency would provide valuable insights into its scalability.
A time comparison between WPDDFormer and UPDDFormer would strengthen the evidence supporting UPDDFormer’s efficiency claims.
The message-passing mechanism and implementation code appears to greatly overlap with ComFormer; the authors should highlight key differences or move overlapping content to background or appendix.
A proper citation and discussion of Zeoformer (referred to as UPDD in the paper) are still necessary.
The method name (UPDD) and the exact methodology are identical to those in Zeoformer, raising concerns about the novelty of the work.
The reliance on Zeoformer and short development timeframe raises concerns about the robustness of the theoretical proofs presented.
The paper does not provide a clear discussion of why the use of pairwise distance distribution resolves atom position fluctuation issues caused by thermal vibrations.
The connection between atomic vibrations and the proposed PDD method is not explicitly established, lacking justification of how the distribution addresses continuous fluctuations.

The current evaluation does not sufficiently isolate the impact of each contribution; more ablation studies are needed to determine whether performance gains stem from the PDD integration, the new transformer architecture, or both.

Incomplete and potentially misleading claims about completeness: the PDD matrix only considers geometric arrangements, disregards atomic types, cannot distinguish structures with identical positions but different compositions, may fail on unstable structures, and cannot differentiate chiral crystals, indicating limitations in the theoretical foundation.
Limited novelty in crystal graph construction: the proposed UPDD crystal graph method is not novel and overlaps with Zeoformer, with insufficient discussion of similarities and differences.
Message passing layers appear largely derived from ComFormer, with only minor modifications, lacking clear articulation of novel aspects or improvements over ComFormer.
The experimentation focuses on relatively simple scalar properties, some of which do not physically depend on crystal periodicity.
Incorporating PDD into crystal graphs makes the data physics-informed, however, the proposed model does not seem to consider interpretability.
In Definition 1, suggest using boldface or other methods to help distinguish scalar, vector, and matrix.
The language in definitions is vague: Line 133, the range of what “crystal graph” refers to should be specified.
The description of geometrical completeness at Line 137 is unclear.
Typos such as Line 129 “and If” and Line 512 “However”.
